stem: A 52-year-old man with a 30 pack-year smoking history, who quit 10 years ago, comes for a routine checkup. He has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate screening test?
expl: USPSTF: annual low-dose CT for adults 50–80 years with ≥20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years. He is 52, 30 pack-years, quit 10 years ago → eligible.

why.B: Sputum cytology isn't a screening test.
why.D: PET is for staging, not screening.

stem: Which of the following can be the candidate for lung cancer screening

opts.t: a 51 year-old male with 30 pack-year smoking
a 52 year-old male with 10 pack-year smoking
a 40 year-old male with 20 pack-year smoking
a 49 year-old male with 20 pack-year smoking

expl: Eligibility = age 50–80 AND ≥20 pack-years (current smoker or quit ≤15 years). Only the 51-year-old with 30 pack-years meets both. (The source writes "correct answer is A".)

stem: Patient with lung cancer, Came to the clinic with headache. You suspect metastasis What is the Best method to invitigate ?
srcNote: (Lung cancer) (pet scan doesn’t show brain Mets so we choose brain mri) Only three answer choices are provided in the source.
expl: Brain metastasis is best shown by contrast MRI of the brain. PET is unreliable in the brain because normal brain tissue is highly glucose-avid; CT is the fallback if MRI can't be done.

why.B: Normal brain uptake hides metastases on PET.
why.C: Less sensitive than MRI (used only if MRI is unavailable).

stem: What is the cut off to call a lung lesion a nodule
expl: A solitary pulmonary nodule is ≤ 3 cm; anything > 3 cm is a mass (more likely malignant).

stem: Which of the following Lung cancers are treated non-surgically?
expl: Small cell carcinoma presents late and disseminates early, so it is treated with chemo-radiotherapy rather than surgery (rare very early SCLC can be resected).

stem: What is the most common presentation of lung cancer?
expl: About 80% of patients are asymptomatic at detection — lung cancer is often found incidentally; symptoms (cough, haemoptysis) are late and nonspecific.

why.A: Common, but less than asymptomatic presentation.

stem: A 65-year-old male heavy smoker diagnosed of early stage Non-small cell lung cancer involving the right lower lobe (T1NOMO). Which one of the following is the operation of choice for this patient?
expl: Early-stage NSCLC (T1N0M0) in a patient fit for surgery → anatomical lobectomy with lymph-node dissection (the standard oncologic operation).

why.B: Wedge resection is non-anatomical — for diagnosis, metastases or patients who can't tolerate lobectomy.
why.C: Pneumonectomy removes far more lung than needed.
why.D: Segmentectomy is reserved for very small tumours or limited pulmonary reserve.

stem: A 65-year-old male patient, chronic smoker, diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer(NSCLC) What is the most accurate statement regarding his staging workup?

opts.t: Video Assisted thoracoscopy (VATS) is used routinely in the diagnosis and staging of lung cancers
Chest MRI has the best advantage over all diagnostic tools
CT scan of the chest is not necessary in staging of (NSCLC) if MRI was done
Mediastinoscopy / mediastinotomy helps in staging of (NSCLC) with accuracy of greater than 90%

srcNote: Source key was A; corrected — see explanation. (Lung tumors-lung cancer)
expl: Mediastinoscopy samples mediastinal nodes directly and stages NSCLC with > 90% accuracy (high tissue yield). The source keyed A, but VATS is not used routinely for diagnosis and staging — it is a resection approach used selectively.

why.B: MRI is not superior to CT/PET-CT for lung cancer (it is used for the brain and superior sulcus tumours).
why.C: CT chest is essential for staging.

stem: What is the wedge resection of the lung best indicated for?
expl: Wedge resection is non-anatomical: it suits diagnosis, benign lesions and pulmonary metastases (e.g. colorectal). Primary lung cancer needs an anatomical resection (lobectomy).

why.A: Sarcoidosis is diagnosed by EBUS/mediastinal biopsy, not wedge resection.

stem: Which ONE of the following lung lesions is a malignant tumor?
expl: Carcinoid tumours are low-grade malignant neuroendocrine tumours (can metastasize). Hamartoma, granular cell tumour and sclerosing haemangioma (pneumocytoma) are benign.

why.C: Benign (the commonest benign lung tumour, "popcorn" calcification).
